content.title: Modifying Mathematical Models
content.overview: This lesson focuses on updating an existing mathematical model when real-world conditions change. You will learn to identify which specific parts of a formula—coefficients or constants—are affected by new information and how to apply those changes precisely to create a revised model.
learning_objectives: Identify which parameters in a linear model represent fixed costs versus variable rates.
Apply fixed-amount changes to the constant term of a model.
Apply percentage-based changes to the coefficients of a model.
Construct a revised algebraic expression based on multiple simultaneous condition changes.

sections.title: The Local-Update Principle
sections.content: When a problem provides an existing model (like C = 15x + 200) and introduces new conditions, you must use the Local-Update Principle. This means you only change the specific parts of the formula mentioned in the new conditions. A standard linear model has two main parts: the coefficient (the number attached to the variable, representing a rate) and the constant (the standalone number, representing a fixed starting value or fee). If a change affects the 'per-unit' cost, update the coefficient. If a change affects a 'flat fee' or 'initial cost,' update the constant.

sections.title: Updating Constants and Coefficients
sections.content: There are two primary ways to update a value: 1. Fixed Adjustments: Add or subtract a specific dollar amount or unit value directly to the constant or coefficient. 2. Percentage Adjustments: To increase a value by p%, multiply it by (1 + p/100). To decrease a value by p%, multiply it by (1 - p/100). For example, a 15% increase is a multiplier of 1.15, while a 15% decrease is a multiplier of 0.85.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Modification Procedure
sections.content:
First, identify the original parameters. Second, determine which parameters are changing and by how much. Third, calculate the new values for those specific parameters. Fourth, rewrite the equation by substituting the new values while keeping all other parts of the original equation exactly the same.

![A flowchart showing the steps to modify a mathematical model: Identify Parameters, Calculate Changes, Substitute Values, and Verify.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/5e476eb6-3ca3-474c-b302-69a04fdbfc63-1786506349234-747.webp)

worked_examples.question: A subscription service models its monthly revenue with R(m) = 45m + 500, where m is the number of members. The company decides to increase the monthly membership fee by 20% and reduce the one-time sign-up fee by $100. What is the revised revenue model?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify original parts. The coefficient (monthly fee) is 45. The constant (sign-up fee) is 500. Step 2: Apply changes. The monthly fee increases by 20%: 45 * 1.20 = 54. The sign-up fee decreases by $100: 500 - 100 = 400. Step 3: Rewrite the model. Replace 45 with 54 and 500 with 400. The revised model is R(m) = 54m + 400.

common_mistakes: Applying a percentage increase to the entire expression instead of just the specific coefficient mentioned.
Confusing the constant (fixed value) with the coefficient (rate per unit).
Forgetting to subtract when a condition specifies a 'reduction' or 'discount'.
Adding a percentage (e.g., + 0.10) instead of multiplying by the growth factor (e.g., * 1.10).
exam_tips: Look for keywords like 'per,' 'each,' or 'every' to identify the coefficient.
Look for keywords like 'flat fee,' 'initial,' or 'fixed' to identify the constant.
Always perform a 'sanity check' by plugging in a simple number like 1 or 10 to see if the new total makes sense compared to the old one.
content.recap: To modify a model, isolate the affected parameters, apply the specific mathematical change (addition/subtraction for fixed amounts or multiplication for percentages), and substitute them back into the original structure.

knowledge_claims.content: In a linear model of the form ax + b, the coefficient 'a' represents the rate per unit and the constant 'b' represents the fixed offset or initial value.
The Local-Update Principle requires changing only the specific parameters mentioned in the new conditions while leaving all other parts of the model unchanged.
To increase a parameter by p%, multiply the original parameter value by the factor (1 + p/100).
To decrease a parameter by p%, multiply the original parameter value by the factor (1 - p/100).
A fixed fee increase is applied by adding the dollar amount directly to the constant term of the linear equation.
Keywords such as 'per unit' or 'hourly rate' indicate that a change should be applied to the coefficient of the variable.
Keywords such as 'one-time fee' or 'base price' indicate that a change should be applied to the constant term.
It is a mistake to multiply the entire original expression by a percentage factor if the change only applies to one specific rate within the model.
A revised model can be verified by substituting a test value for the variable and comparing the result to the original model's output to ensure the change is proportional to the description.
If a model C(x) = 10x + 50 is updated to C(x) = 10x + 60, the change represents a $10 increase in fixed costs with no change to the variable rate.
If a model C(x) = 10x + 50 is updated to C(x) = 11x + 50, the change represents a 10% increase in the variable rate with no change to fixed costs.
When multiple conditions change simultaneously, calculate each new parameter value independently before assembling the final revised expression.

items.stem:
Practice form 1.
A linear model underpredicts every new value by about 2. Which revision is most reasonable?
A) decrease the intercept by 2
B) reverse the sign of every input
C) increase the intercept by about 2
D) remove the dependent variable

options.B: reverse the sign of every input

items.explanation: A consistent vertical underprediction suggests an intercept adjustment.

videoLesson.title: Modify Model By Updating Coefficients
videoLesson.description: Recognize which variables, coefficients, or constants the new condition changes. Update only affected terms by adding or subtracting fixed amounts or multiplying coefficients by percent factors.
